title: Through the Panama Canal
hook: A ship sails from the Atlantic into the Pacific. Which way does it head?

knows: that the Panama Canal links the Atlantic and the Pacific
doesNotKnow: which way a ship heads through the canal
that the Pacific end is east of the Atlantic end

misconception: Going from the Atlantic to the Pacific through the canal means sailing west.
objective: The learner can say that a ship going from the Atlantic to the Pacific through the canal heads south-east overall (about 142 degrees), because the isthmus runs east-west.

claims.text: The canal's Atlantic end is at Colon (9.36 N, 79.90 W) and its Pacific end at Balboa (8.95 N, 79.57 W).
claims.source: From memory, not re-checked: approximate gazetteer coordinates of the Colon/Cristobal and Balboa terminals (brief cites the Panama Canal Authority or a gazetteer). The stage uses exactly these points. On the kit's 1:110m outline the Colon point falls just off the coast, which is expected at that resolution.

claims.text: The straight-line heading from the Atlantic end to the Pacific end is about 142 degrees (south-east).
claims.source: Builder's node check, initial great-circle bearing from the Colon point to the Balboa point: 141.50 degrees, shown rounded as 142 (the brief gives 140.9 from slightly different coordinates). Computed by the same bearing() as the stage.

claims.text: The straight line between the two ends is about 58 km long, and the Pacific end is 0.33 degrees of longitude east of the Atlantic end.
claims.source: Builder's node check: geoDistance x 6,371.0088 km = 58.2 km; -79.57 - (-79.90) = 0.33 degrees. The canal's own length is longer; the lesson says 'straight line'.

claims.text: Panama's isthmus curves like an S, running east-west, so the Pacific end of the canal is further east than the Atlantic end.
claims.source: From the brief (cm-geography). Consistent with c1 and c3. The kit's Panama outline shows the east-west run. Not independently checked by the builder.

claims.text: The canal winds, so the stated heading is its overall direction, not every turn.
claims.source: From the brief: the bearing is between terminals, not the canal's own course; the canal's winding is from memory.

claims.text: On a Mercator map compass bearings are true angles, so a heading can be read directly (north up).
claims.source: Snyder (1987), ch. 7: Mercator is conformal, so angles are preserved. Already verified for mercator-greenland c5. Stage is labelled Mercator, zoomed on Panama.

recall.question: Going from the Atlantic to the Pacific through the Panama Canal, you head mostly...
recall.why: The isthmus runs east-west, so the Pacific end is south-east of the Atlantic end (about 142 degrees).
